title: Log Context Enrichment & Evidence Packaging Playbook
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes standard conventions for enriching runtime logs with minimal, high-value context and for packaging those enriched logs into audit-grade evidence bundles for investigations, compliance requests, and cross-border audits. The guidance is designed to minimize PII exposure while preserving forensic utility.

Audience: Security engineers, SREs, platform engineers, privacy/compliance reviewers, incident responders.

Scope

This document covers:
- What contextual fields must be added to all request/operation audit logs produced by Redwood services.
- How to transform and redact sensitive fields for evidence packages.
- The step-by-step evidence packaging workflow for incidents and compliance requests.
- Roles, ownership and retention mapping for packaged artifacts.

Out of scope: endpoint application logs with business-level PII that are owned by product teams; those teams must map to this playbook for evidence extraction.

Principles

1) Need-to-investigate context only: include fields that materially speed triage (actor, action, resource, request_id, model_id, region, decision flags).
2) Immutable provenance: every evidence bundle MUST include a signed manifest and the original immutable audit shard identifiers.
3) Privacy-first: PII must be redacted at source where possible; if raw PII is required for legal hold it must follow a separate legal request workflow.
4) Reproducibility: evidence packages should contain enough deterministic signals to reproduce routing and authorization decisions.

Roles and responsibilities

- Service owner: ensure instrumented services emit the required context fields and follow redaction rules.
- Logging platform (Observability team): supply enrichment transforms and a canonical enrichment library; own storage TTLs and immutable shard IDs.
- Security forensics lead: assemble evidence bundles, attest to redaction steps, sign the manifest, and own chain-of-custody notes.
- Legal/Privacy: approve release of any PII-heavy evidence and own external disclosures.

Required enrichment schema (minimum set)

All enriched audit logs must include (flat fields):
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- service_name (e.g., redwood-serving-v2)
- env (production|staging|dev)
- request_id (UUID v4)
- trace_id (opentelemetry)
- actor_type (service|user|job)
- actor_id (obfuscated, see redaction rules)
- auth_method (api_key|oauth|mTLS|internal-token)
- auth_role (role name assigned by RBAC)
- resource_type (model|route|snapshot|dataset)
- resource_id (stable ID)
- operation (generate|embed|deploy|rollback|config-change)
- model_variant (if applicable)
- region (aws-us-west-2|gcp-europe-west1|onprem-lon1)
- latency_ms (end-to-end)
- decision_flags (list of short codes for routing/fallbacks)
- kvcache_hit (true|false)
- batch_size (int)
- token_count (int)

Redaction and obfuscation rules

- actor_id: store hashed(actor_id, salt=org-secret) in logs by default. If an incident requires a cleartext mapping, the security forensics lead performs a controlled lookup against the identity store and records the lookup in the evidence manifest.
- request payloads: strip full user prompts unless explicitly requested under legal hold; instead include prompt fingerprint (sha256) and tokenized length.
- embeddings and model outputs: store only derived hashes for ephemeral outputs unless retention is required by a compliance request.

Evidence packaging workflow (high level)

1) Trigger: Incident Response or Compliance Request opens an evidence collection ticket (IR#{id}) in the incident system.
2) Scope and TTL: Security forensics lead sets the collection scope (time range, services, actor filters) and an evidence TTL (default 365 days for incident-related bundles unless legal hold applies).
3) Immutable shard selection: Logging platform exports immutable shards covering the time range. Shards are identified by shard_id and content-hash.
4) Enrichment replay: Using the canonical enrichment library, replay logs into an "evidence view" that performs redaction transforms as configured.
5) Artifact assembly: Package includes: immutable shards (read-only copy), enriched evidence view (ndjson), manifest.json (signed), chain_of_custody.txt, and an access-control policy snapshot.
6) Attestation: Forensics lead signs manifest with internal code-signing key and records the attestation in the evidence ticket.
7) Delivery: Provide the bundle to requestor via secure transfer (S3 signed-url with KMS envelope) and record all ACL changes.

Detailed runbook: incident evidence capture (step-by-step)

1) Intake (T+0–T+4 hours)
   a) Confirm ticket ID and owner.
   b) Capture scope: earliest_start_timestamp, latest_end_timestamp, primary service(s), actor filters, and whether PII cleartext is authorized.

2) Prepare exports (T+4–T+12 hours)
   a) Ask Logging platform to mark and snapshot immutable shards covering the time range.
   b) Record shard_ids and content-hash in the ticket.

3) Execute enrichment replay (T+12–T+24 hours)
   a) Run canonical enrichment tool with parameters: --scope-file ticket_scope.json --redaction-level standard | restricted.
   b) Output: evidence-view.ndjson (newline-delimited JSON) and a transform-log.txt describing any dropped fields.

4) Assemble artifact (T+24–T+36 hours)
   a) Create directory: evidence_bundle/IR#{id}/
   b) Add: shards.tar (immutable shards), evidence-view.ndjson, manifest.json (see manifest template below), chain_of_custody.txt, access_snapshot.json, and a README.txt with TL;DR.
   c) Sign manifest.json using the forensics signing key and store signature alongside manifest.

5) Approve and deliver (T+36–T+48 hours)
   a) Forensic lead signs off and Legal verifies PII decisions.
   b) Deliver via secure channel and update ticket with link, expiry, and recipients.

Manifest template (fields must be present)

| field | description |
|---|---|
| bundle_id | IR#{id} or CR#{id} |
| created_by | forensics lead name |
| created_at | ISO8601 UTC |
| shard_ids | comma-separated list of shard_id|
| shard_hashes | comma-separated list of content-hashes |
| enrichment_version | semantic version of enrichment library used |
| redaction_level | standard|restricted|none |
| signature_key_id | key id used to sign manifest |
| files | comma-separated list of files in bundle |
| access_policy_snapshot | path to access snapshot file |
| retention_until | ISO8601 UTC |

Retention and access mapping

The following binding table maps evidence types to default retention and access class. Teams may request extensions via the risk-exceptions process.

| artifact_type | default_retention | access_class | owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| immutable_shards | 3 years | restricted | Observability |
| evidence_view_ndjson | 365 days | restricted | Security Forensics |
| manifest.json + signature | 7 years | restricted | Security Forensics |
| chain_of_custody.txt | 10 years | restricted | Legal/Security |
| access_snapshot.json | 3 years | internal | Observability |

Access control and RBAC interactions

- Evidence bundles are stored in the evidence S3 bucket with bucket-level encryption and object-level RBAC.
- Access to bundles must be granted by the Security forensics lead via a short-lived grant mechanism (IAM role assumption with timebound session).
- All access events to evidence bundles are logged into the immutable audit stream and linked to the evidence manifest.

Verification and audit checklist

Before closing an evidence ticket, verify:
- [ ] Shard content-hash matches manifest entries.
- [ ] Manifest signature verified against current key-id in the signing key registry.
- [ ] Redaction transforms are documented in transform-log.txt.
- [ ] Chain-of-custody contains at least: collector name, timestamps, storage hash, and recipient approvals.
- [ ] Delivery link has expiry and recipient recorded in ticket.

Operational patterns and automations

- Canonical enrichment library: A single library (language: Go/Python) will be maintained in the observability mono-repo. Changes require a changelog and automated replay tests against synthetic traffic prior to release.
- Evidence bundle automation: A serverless workflow will orchestrate shard export, enrichment replay, bundle assembly, and signature. Manual steps remain for legal attestation and final delivery.
- Monitoring: Dashboard showing pending evidence requests, average fulfillment time, and percentage of bundles with PII escalation. SLO target: 95% of evidence bundles assembled within 48 hours of request.

Appendix: sample log (ndjson line)

{"timestamp_utc":"2026-11-01T15:42:10.123Z","service_name":"redwood-serving-v2","env":"production","request_id":"8a2f9cfa-...","trace_id":"00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"sha256:7b5f...","auth_method":"api_key","auth_role":"data-reader","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"rwd-model-7","operation":"generate","model_variant":"quant4x","region":"aws-us-west-2","latency_ms":78,"decision_flags":"fallback_to_small","kvcache_hit":false,"batch_size":1,"token_count":34}

CLI examples

# Request immutable shards (example)
redwood-logs export --start 2026-10-31T00:00:00Z --end 2026-11-01T23:59:59Z --service redwood-serving-v2 --output shards.tar

# Run enrichment replay (example)
enrich-playback --input shards.tar --schema v1 --redaction standard --output evidence-view.ndjson
